newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end down on retail liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end down on retail liquidation.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down on Tuesday due to liquidation by retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded November 1997 contract ended at 3,278 yuan ($395) per tonne, losing 12 yuan. It opened at 3,275 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 3,274 and a high of 3,279.
July fell 103 to 3,157, September 17 to 3,258, the January 1998 contract fell two to 3,240 and March was unchanged at 3,300 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 18,300 tonnes from 22,000 tonnes.
Most contracts opened lower and moved around the opening level for most of the session, traders said.
"Liquidation of long positions by retail investors dominated today's trading because investors are pessimistic about the short-term market trend," one trader said.
"Technical charts showed soybean futures gradually drifting away from the 3,300 yuan level," he said.
A lack of market-moving news meant investors were reluctant to buy, traders said, adding that the active stock markets had been attracting speculative funds away from soybean futures.
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate in the next few days.
